findings: critical

Fail-open: a reviewer error or invalid/drifted verdict now returns 0 (pass) instead of 2 (block), so an outage, timeout, or unparseable response is treated as a clean review and unreviewed code or deploys go through. (1) The attacker needs only to make the reviewer call fail or return malformed output (network outage, killed process, schema drift, output that breaks parsing); no config or code access is needed. (2) They get a full bypass of the blocking review gate for every plugin user, with no audit record of the skip. (3) Cheapest fix: revert to `return 2` on `result.error or not result.valid`. Full fix: also add a regression test that asserts error and invalid results both block, with an audit entry. (gate.py:11)

No test covers the changed error/invalid branch, so a fail-closed to fail-open flip like this one merges without any test going red. (1) The attacker needs no prior control; this is a missing safeguard. (2) Future regressions of the same class go undetected. (3) Cheapest fix: a parametrized test asserting `check_review` returns 2 for `error=True` and for `valid=False`, including when `blocking=False`. Full fix: add that test to a mutation-checked guard suite. (gate.py:10)
critical

Config `exclude` is checked before `HARD_PATHS`, so `.codex-gate.yaml` can remove hard code paths from the gate. (1) The attacker must already be able to write, or leave unstaged, an edit to `.codex-gate.yaml`, which any repo committer can do. (2) Any hard path, including the gate's own scripts, stops being treated as code, so commits skip the ladder and review silently: the fail-open "weakening via config" case AGENTS.md forbids. (3) Cheapest fix: move the `HARD_PATHS` check above the `exclude` check so exclusions can never override hard paths. Full fix: also reject or ignore `exclude` entries that match `HARD_PATHS`, and read `exclude` only from the HEAD/staged config, not the worktree. (gate.py:20)

An excluded path skips the gate with no audit record. (1) The attacker needs the same config write access as above. (2) Code-path skips leave no trace in the audit log, so the bypass cannot be seen or investigated afterwards. (3) Cheapest fix: write an audit entry with the path and the matching `exclude` rule whenever `exclude` returns False. Full fix: route every non-code decision driven by config through the audited skip mechanism. (gate.py:20-21)

The new `exclude` branch has no test showing it cannot override `HARD_PATHS`. (1) Nothing is needed; this is a regression risk. (2) A future change could reintroduce the override without any test turning red. (3) Cheapest fix: add one test where `exclude` contains a `HARD_PATHS` entry and assert the result is True. Full fix: add tests for a missing config, a broken config, and a non-list `exclude`, each asserting strict behaviour. (gate.py:20)

`exclude` entries are compared as raw strings with no normalization or type check. (1) The attacker needs control of config contents. (2) A string instead of a list, a non-list type, or odd path forms produce unpredictable membership results. If `config` is None, `.get` raises, and it is unclear whether callers treat that exception as blocking or as clean. (3) Cheapest fix: normalize both sides with a repo-relative path helper and require `exclude` to be a list of strings, otherwise fail closed. Full fix: validate the config schema up front, with strict defaults when the config is missing or broken. (gate.py:20)
critical

Config-sourced `command` now reaches `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`; this is the AGENTS.md security-class sink (the 25.07 `_run_empirical` finding) and a fail-open path to arbitrary code execution. (1) The attacker only needs write access to the config value, such as an unstaged or repo-committed `.codex-gate.yaml` edit or a PR touching it. No local code execution is needed. (2) They get full shell interpretation (`;`, `&&`, `$(...)`, backticks, redirection) and run arbitrary commands as the gate user. That lets them bypass or forge gate verdicts, write outside the repo, and tamper with ledgers and audit. (3) Cheapest fix: revert to `shlex.split(config['command'])` with `shell=False`. Full fix: accept `command` only as a YAML list (argv), reject strings, and resolve `argv[0]` against a trusted-binary allowlist rather than repo-local paths. (runner.py:5)
medium

No test covers the changed execution path. Add a regression test asserting that a command containing shell metacharacters (for example `true; touch <tmp>/pwned`) is not interpreted and creates no file. The test must use a harmless, nonexistent-target payload per R-GUARD-TEST-MUST-BE-HARMLESS-UNARMED. (1) Nothing further is needed; this is a process gap. (2) The shell=True regression can come back silently. (3) Cheapest fix: one parametrized test on `run()` with a metachar payload. Full fix: a lint/CI rule banning `shell=True` in the gate package. Removing 'gpt-5.6-sol' leaves the blocking panel with only the Anthropic family, so Claude-authored code is judged by Claude alone.
